newsitem.title: USA: Boise says Q2 reflects weak paper prices.
newsitem.headline: Boise says Q2 reflects weak paper prices.

text.p: Boise Cascade Corp said second quarter results reflect continuing weak paper prices, which rose only slightly from the trough levels of the first quarter and were significantly lower than those of a year ago.
"The company's paper business is expected to post stronger results in the second half of 1997," said George Harad, chief executive officer, noting improving industry fundamentals.

Harad said Boise Cascade's office products business should likewise record stronger second-half results, as sales continue to grow, paper prices gradually rise, and recently won national accounts mature.
For the second quarter, Boise reported a net loss of $16.2 million, or $0.53 per fully diluted share for the second quarter of 1997.
This compares with net losses of $17.0 million, or $.55 cents per fully diluted share in the year-ago second quarter and $15.2 million, or $0.51 per fully diluted share in the first quarter.
Sales rose to $1.33 billion from $1.26 billion a year ago.
